subtasks.title: Admit and execute bounded, conversation-bound prompt submissions in order
subtasks.context: The terminal preserves Unicode, literal newlines and bracketed paste, but promptAdmission reserves only one idle prompt and session.go refuses busy follow-ups. E2 established independently verified committed-waiting admission and saved initial-prompt priority. Extend that shared path while preserving startup, permission and ownership safeguards.
changes: Represent complete submissions in one observable acceptance order with bounded resource use and explicit refusal when capacity or eligibility prevents admission.
Bind accepted submissions to current launch and confirmed conversation at acceptance; preserve complete text and submission identity independent from later ACP request IDs.
Run ordinary submissions FIFO, one active prompt, after prior turn and outstanding decision constraints permit progression.
Reuse reporter.verifyReport, runtime/pane verification and durable request predicates; preserve committed-waiting handoff and saved initial-prompt priority.
Separate ordinary submissions from permission/plan choices and controls. Keep /clear and /new visibly refused in Task1.
Preserve public send-keys/read-pane/pause contracts; no new public Cursor control API.
acceptance: Human typing, bracketed paste and successive multiline API submissions preserve Unicode/newlines as distinct complete prompts without duplication or carried text.
Follow-ups accepted during a running turn execute FIFO without cancelling that turn.
No submission starts against an unconfirmed, changed, retired or mismatched launch/conversation; input consumed before startup eligibility cannot become future work after startup.
Committed-waiting reservation survives the hook tail; saved initial prompt retains priority.
Still-open permission/plan decisions block dispatch. Turn completion, acknowledgement, native claim or pipe output cannot manufacture proof that unknown-origin requests are gone.
Saturation explicitly refuses without silently dropping/replacing accepted work or indefinitely blocking work/controls.
Pending, pane-hash, permission-answer and dialog safeguards remain effective.

subtasks.title: Prioritize interruption and shutdown with finite, explicit queue cancellation
subtasks.context: Current interruption/local exit/eligible pause retain a fixed three-second cancellation deadline. Queuing creates races between input consumption, turn completion, pending output and cancellation; bounded shared input channel and synchronous reports require attention. In-memory request retirement is not durable proof a dialog disappeared.
changes: Give interruption and terminal controls priority over waiting ordinary submissions while retaining observable input order.
Cancel active work, retire outstanding decision-response authority and visibly identify each affected not-started submission cancellation.
Prevent input consumed during cancellation from automatically restarting work later.
Preserve the first cancellation deadline through repeated interruption, policy cancellation and authorization-hold release.
Integrate queue cancellation with local exit, eligible pause, signals, transport/runtime failure and owned shutdown.
Prevent accepted outbound prompts from starting after cancellation; treat partial/uncertain output honestly, no retry or false zero-delivery assertion.
Reuse requestController, guarded serialized writer and owned termination/reporting. Unknown-origin durable holds require existing valid proof or owning-spawn end.
acceptance: Interrupt cancels active and affected not-started work, preserves conversation identity, never automatically restarts work.
Controls remain effective under ordinary-input/outbound pressure; cancelled queued prompts never later produce prompt calls.
Repeated interrupts and hold release cannot extend the existing three-second cancellation deadline.
Cancellation retires queued allow and deny while preserving ack-before-output, both guards, bounded store acquisition/post-wait checks and no uncertain replay.
Menu choices cannot answer retired requests; independent question denial retains semantics.
Exit is never model text; exit/eligible pause visibly cancel queue and report ended only after confirmed owned-runtime termination.
Kill/crash cannot restore transient work; caller restart or attach/detach alone preserves gateway/conversation.
Public pause/dialog guards and Claude/Codex behavior remain unchanged.

subtasks.title: Record the complete submission lifecycle in the protected transcript
subtasks.context: Existing private JSONL recorder sequences, attributes and synchronizes records, but user_input is written only when a turn starts. Accepted queued work cancelled before start needs durable observable ordering without a replayable queue.
changes: Extend existing record vocabulary to correlate acceptance, start, cancellation, refusal where applicable, updates and outcomes.
Preserve admission-time launch/life/connection/conversation attribution and correlate started submissions with actual ACP requests.
Distinguish accepted-unstarted, started, cancelled and uncertain outcomes without conflating enqueue, pipe output, receipt or completion.
Preserve protected path/file identity/synchronous persistence; visibly stop further unrecordable admission/dispatch on failure with honest termination.
Keep transient recovery disabled; reuse recorder/lifecycle correlation in Task2 without rotation/history migration here.
acceptance: Reader can reconstruct acceptance order and disposition of every accepted submission, including cancelled-unstarted work.
Exact Unicode/newline text remains attributed to its accepted conversation.
Acceptance/execution order agree for ordinary FIFO work; intervening controls/cancellations identifiable.
No fabricated admission/completion/decision-delivery/saved-history success after persistence failure.
Transcript replacement/symlink/access/write/sync failures retain protected visible handling.
Crashed/interrupted transient work is never replayed; existing references stay truthful.
No new transcript format/public reader/schema migration absent concrete implementation need.

cross_component_findings: Immediate Task1 interface gate before Task2.
requestController.open and cancel are in-memory state, insufficient alone as durable FIFO dispatch eligibility or proof.
Controls must remain effective despite capacity-32 input channel and synchronous report/transcript work.
Cancelling only application queue can leave a late outbound-prompt send race.
SendKeysPane literal text and Enter are separate calls; no unsupported claim of atomic arbitrary concurrent caller submissions.
Reuse cursorfix single runtime, terminal/report/request/proof tests and newCursorPaneScenario. Zero-byte assertions require Raw, not only Frames.
Task1 current docs retain clear/new refusal; Task2 owns rotation/history atomicity; Task3 owns final public/adversarial collector.
Assess queue transitions against existing hold/admission models; no model gap demonstrated or TLA run warranted solely by research.
